notes.title: The First Spine, Arena: a recap of what’s been shared
notes.content: [p]Over the past few months, we revealed the shape of our upcoming online board-and-card game. With a planned release in Q3 2026 and a five-month Early Access phase, the game is beginning to take form through a steady stream of thoughtful updates. This article gathers what’s been announced so far, offering a clear picture of what you can expect.[/p][h2]The core concept: strategy on a living grid[/h2][p]At its heart, The First Spine - Arena is a tactical duel between two wizards. Each match unfolds on a 7×7 grid, where players summon creatures, cast spells, and place artifacts. But the board isn’t just a backdrop, it’s part of the strategy. Lava tiles punish careless movement, water slows progress, and ditches can be used for cover or control. Players can even customize the layout, adding a layer of unpredictability to each encounter.[/p][p]Cards in this game aren’t just actions, they are entities. Once placed, they move, attack, and interact with the board. This transforms each match into a layered puzzle, where positioning and timing matter as much as the cards themselves.[/p][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Gif_3_1_7217dfbcfb.gif"][/img][/p][h2]Progression and crafting: earning your power[/h2][p]Rather than handing out power arbitrarily, The First Spine Arena ties card generation to player level. This means that every new card feels appropriate to your current experience. After each match, players receive cards and resources that allow them to forge new creatures and artifacts to add to their decks.[/p][p]The forge system is built around blueprints, which players can discover and use with Ancient Shards. They can also create new spells from deciphering Fated Knowledges.[/p][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Gif_2_dd4df619b4.gif"][/img][/p][h2]Fair competition: matchmaking and seasonal play[/h2][p]The game’s matchmaking system is designed to pair players with opponents of similar level, creating fair and competitive duels. Whether you’re just starting out or climbing the ranked ladder, you’ll face challenges that test your strategy, not your wallet.[/p][p]Seasonal events will introduce new rules, quests, and rotating leaderboards. These changes are meant to keep the game fresh and encourage players to adapt their decks and tactics over time.[/p][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Gif_1_ec6a8b3da8.gif"][/img][/p][h2]A collaborative approach[/h2][p]We made it clear that the Early Access phase is more than a testing phase, it’s a chance to build the game alongside our community. Feedback will shape everything from card balance to new features, and players will be credited for their contributions. It’s a collaborative model that values input and iteration over perfection.[/p][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Gif_4_2_aa69c4a6bc.gif"][/img][/p][p]You can wishlist Arena here if you want to take part of that journey:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3307700/The_First_Spine__Arena/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Arena: a new way to play online against other players on Steam
notes.content:
[p]Get ready to enter the Arena, the thrilling new way to experience The First Spine online! Compete head-to-head, showcase your skills, and rise through the ranks in this exciting competitive mode.[/p][p]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3307700/The_First_Spine__Arena/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h1]Each card is unique[/h1][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Image_Sequence_013_0160_639d50e368.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In Arena, no two decks are alike. Don’t expect to wield the same cards as your opponents, every card is uniquely generated based on your level, giving you a personalized arsenal tailored to your journey.[/p][p]From the color scheme to the stats, each card is crafted to reflect your progress, making your deck as unique as your playstyle.[/p][h1]Level-based matchmaking and different lobbys[/h1][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Image_Sequence_001_0000_9410f664f9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Join distinct lobbies, each of them truely unique. As you earn XP, new locations unlock, each with its own unique twist: flooded board, destructible cards, and strategic challenges that push your gameplay to the next level.[/p][p]The first release of Arena features five thrilling locations, each offering exclusive cards rewards tailored to their environment.[/p][p]And when it comes to matchmaking, we keep it fair and fierce. You’ll face opponents at your level, with decks balanced in power. Victory comes down to strategy, not stats.[/p][h1]There is more than one way to obtain new cards[/h1][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Image_Sequence_003_0007_0598a5925d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Every battle in Arena brings knowledge and not just victory. Earn two powerful forms of wisdom: Ancient Knowledge and Fated Knowledge.[/p][p]Use Ancient Knowledge to forge new cards, then supercharge them with Ancient Shards. The more shards you invest, the stronger your card becomes.[/p][p]Fated Knowledge unlocks mysterious spells. Once deciphered by a character, each type reveals one spell from a pool of 2 to 4 possibilities, adding an element of surprise to your journey.[/p][h1]This is The First Spine, with new rules[/h1][p][img src="https://cms.thefirstspine.fr/uploads/Image_Sequence_002_0000_0bf0c68932.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This is The First Spine. This is our board game reimagined for the online world. It’s everything you love about strategic gameplay, now supercharged with ladders, quests, and unique cards that evolve with you.[/p][p]We’ve poured our passion into every detail, and we hope you’ll feel that energy as you play. Dive in, compete, explore, and enjoy the journey as much as we loved creating it![/p]

notes.title: After the recast
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

After the release of the recasted version of Drifter’s Tales, it’s time for us to talk more about what’s next.

[b]What’s next for Drifter’s Tales[/b]

We are currently working on porting the game on a console (the platform is yet to announce) and on mobile. Those versions should be launched during the first half of 2025.

In the meantime, we are also working on a DLC that will be offered to our players prior to the release of it. This DLC will take place at the same location of the initial version with all the new mechanics we introduced in the recast. The DLC is dated to mid-2025.

[b]What’s next for The First Spine[/b]

Drifter’s Tales is a game finding its roots from The First Spine, a cards game we presented in various festivals and conferences in Europe. You can play online to this game on your browser.

We decided to rework this version too, with a client developed as the same way as Drifter’s Tales. We will share more details soon, but know that this game will also be available on Steam.

notes.title: Discover the new features of the recasted version
notes.content:
Along with the demo we released a few days back, we prepared you a short video presenting you all the changes to come in the recasted version.

[previewyoutube=yNadvfCmThc;full][/previewyoutube]

As a reminder, here's a list of those changes:

[b]A brand-new story[/b]

You will be able to try a brand-new story, which will take you to the continent of Carmina, full of legends and threats. During your playthrough, you will have to choose your own path to your main objective. We are not sharing many details about the story, but we are excited about this one!

Know that one playthrough won't be enough to discover all the stories - some will be available according your choices, and all of them will change on the NG+. Ah yes, a NG+ mode is fully integrated in the recasted version.

[b]New gameplay[/b]

In the initial version, you must pick from a card to another to move around. In the recasted version, you will be able to move a pawn on a map and pick the card you want to. It will allow you to move around quickly and not waste time on cards you already have read.

The battles were also fully rebranded. We increased the readability of them, allowing you to move the point of view on the game board. Plus, some enemy moves require you to avoid projectiles and draw rune to test your reflexes and dexterity.

[b]New cards, new ways to obtain them[/b]

30+ new cards. Not less! You character will be able to create new cards at the end of each story and will have to remember some lost memories to unlock more cards.

We have added more cards in the chests and more random encounters and each story has a secret card you will have to discover.

Finally, some cards will be hidden behind legends to read on the story selection screen. These cards are powerful and will change your build if you find them!

[b]New customization features[/b]

We are also proposing you to customize your player cards by increasing their stats. Those customizations will be available with a new character, the "Alchemist". He will help you to create potions from some ingredients you could loot around.

[b]Economy balancing[/b]

Finally, we have balanced the economy. Thanks to this balancing, you can buy more cards and build a real deck for breaking your enemies. And if you run out of gems... you can destroy some cards to earn some more.

[b]Quality of life improvements[/b]

We integrated too some QOL improvements in the recasted version:
- full mouse / keyboard / gamepad support without choosing a mode
- battles / exploration / return to checkpoints without any loading
- file-based save system for the masters who want to edit their saves
- mods support
- performances improvements

notes.title: Drifter's Tales won't participate in the Next Fest and will not have a relaunch
notes.content:
[i]TL;DR Steam has unilaterally decided to cancel our relaunch, canceling our participation to the Next Fest at the same time. We are working on a solution to not abandon our players. [/i]

A few hours ago, Steam informed us of their cancellation of our relaunch. It is with a broken heart that we write these lines, because their simple decision has big consequences on the last year of work we have done to give you the update you deserve. 

We initially had to release this relaunch under a new page to have a fresh start and take advantage of the features that Steam offers to new games: 

[list]
[*] The possibility of launching a demo before the release of the game 
[*] Participation in the Steam Next Fest 
[*] A boost in visibility at launch 
[/list]

The relaunch page was validated by Steam on June 24th, 2023 and we began marketing operations to ensure enough wishlists for the launch. 

We informed on December 2nd of our desire to upload a new game while sending Steam keys to the buyers of the initial version. Steam told us that we cannot send keys to people who have already purchased the original game. In the interest of fairness, we decided to send keys to our entire community as well as to people who contacted us on our support channels, while offering free DLC covering the story of the original game with reworked mechanics. 

On January 10th, a few minutes after completing our demo, Steam without explanation placed the relaunch page back in “rewiew”. This is not supposed to happen - once the page is validated, the concept itself is validated by Steam. A few days later, Steam informed us that we no longer had authorization to release the relaunch. 

This has serious consequences for us, as well as our community: 

[list]
[*] Despite our efforts to address all community comments during the relaunch, we will keep the - justified - comments from players from the initial version forever 
[*] The relaunch will not be able to take advantage of events such as Steam Next Fest, as well as the press coverage associated with it 
[*] We will not be able to take advantage of the launch boost offered by Steam for new games 
[*] The release plan as well as the marketing plan that we have put in place must be completely redone, and we are losing all our efforts on the new page – along with the wishlists on it 
[/list]

We are currently working on a solution to provide you with this new version – because you deserve it. Our players are the reason for our game, and it is our mission to deliver the results of this past year. 

We will come back to you in a few days with a solution and an update plan that will be done on the game you already own. Because even if we are the losers in Steam's unilateral decision, there is no reason that our players should be losers too. 

Regards, 

Teddy

notes.title: Happy holidays from us!
notes.content:
[h1]We are wishing you happy holidays, full of games and rest![/h1]

2024 will be for us the launch of the new Drifter's Tales version, full of improvements.

As the game is now finished and we are polishing it, we are able to give you a complete list of what  will change in the upcoming version:

[h3]A brand new story[/h3]

We will present you a brand-new story. It's not an update - it's a completely new journey. As an architect, healer, priest or blacksmith you will have to travel to another country.

In a complete playthrough you won't be able to play all the stories we have prepared for you - at the end of each story, you will have to choose your next story. You can play 5 stories in a playthrough among the 11 available.

Each story as its own secrets and characteristics, and we hope you will enjoy all the efforts we have put on it to vary the situations each time!

[h3]More cards, more mods[/h3]

Obviously, we added more cards in the game. There will be 31 new cards available!

We also added new ways to obtain the cards in your journey:
- as you have now an origin (architect, healer, priest or blacksmith), you will be able to obtain 12 cards from it
- you can hear stories from The Storyteller, rewarding you a card each time
- we added also new covenants, and new secrets

We introduced also new mods to mod your cards, and also your character! Yes, thanks to the Alchemy you will be able to increase the stats of your own character.

[h3]Revamped battles[/h3]

The battle system was fully revamped. Now the enemies can play multiple time, and you won't be inactive anymore during their turn! You will have to avoid projectiles and draw runes with your keyboard/gamepad to survive.

Also, some battlefields will have squares with various effects (lava, water, hole) - you will be able to use it at your advantages with some cards, it's up to your strategy!

[h3]We learnt from our failure[/h3]

During the launch of the previous game, many of you pointed out the lack of mouse support. Now, you are able to play with your mouse, the keyboard of your gamepad (Xbox or DualShock controllers).

Also, some may have found that the game missed some replay value. Now, the New Game Plus mode is part of the experience, and will offer you the opportunity to refine your decks from a playthrough to another.

We hope you will like this new chapter, which you can wishlist here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2366490/DRIFTERS_TALES__A_narrative_board_game/

notes.title: Dev diary #7: Deep dive in the very first moments of the game
notes.content:
Hello everyone ! Last time we shared a few tricks that we use to make every fight in Drifter's Tales as epic as possible. Today we are going to reveal the first moments in the game.

And yes, it's time for you to find out how your adventure will begin!

Don't forget to wishlist us on Steam here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2366490/DRIFTERS_TALES__A_narrative_board_game/ 

[b]At the origin of everything[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021240/d2d72681fd8729bf1b15ad807dcb716059c920bd.gif[/img]

The very first step of your journey will introduce you to one of the biggest new features compared to the original game. Your character has a story!

This origin will be chosen randomly from 4 available: Healer, Blacksmith, Architect or Priest. Each story will allow you to gradually unlock new cards. For example, the Architect will be able to modify the game board while the Blacksmith will improve his cards to make them stronger and more resistant!

Drifter’s Tales has a fairly significant replay value. Because in addition to having this origin, you will have to choose a path and play 6 stories among the 12 available in a single run. And if you want to try another path your run, you can try it with the New Game + mode.

[b]Buy a ticket to Carmina[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021240/c45c231e871f7f36c57146f66b3c259396ef8947.gif[/img]

Whatever your origin, you will have to board the Victoire which will take you to Carmina, the new region covered in this game.

Not far from this vendor, a secret will be revealed to you, allowing you to enhance your deck with a new card. Because yes, we have stuffed the game with secrets of all kinds! The covenants will no longer be the only puzzles to solve, you will have to be attentive and think outside the box to complete your collection of cards.

[b]The first battle[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021240/7b3782c803c0bc482e45039ec64c73b1d7f020d0.gif[/img]

Arriving in Carmina, you will have to very quickly lead your first fight against “Someone”. Your hand will be predefined and each stage of the fight will be explained to you as you go.

We focused on clarity in this part of the game by overhauling the entire combat system. Camera movements will accompany your actions to allow you to concentrate on the action in progress.

You will notice in the gif that accompanies this article that there is no loading between combat and exploration occurs. Everything is fluid, and we are very happy with the transition effects that accompany the state changes between exploration & combat!

[b]Aside: Steam Next Fest & Twitch streams[/b]

We will be participating in the Steam Next Fest from October 9th to 16th. This will be the opportunity for you to download a demo of the game containing the first 3 stories. We have also integrated feedback from our alpha tests into this demo (and we thank you for your valuable feedback!)

Finally, you will be able to participate in the development of the game on Twtich because we stream certain development sessions here: https://www.twitch.tv/teddydeveloppeunjeu

notes.title: Dev diary #6: How to make cards battles epics?
notes.content:
One of the challenges we faced was of course to answer the following question: how to create a cards game that contains epic fights?

This article is the sixth devlog for our relaunch of Drifter's Tales, a narrative board game available on Steam in early 2024 here: 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2366490/DRIFTERS_TALES__A_narrative_board_game/

[b]Impactful visual effects[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/1f0439805864250168516439d3495cb73c837be1.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/a1b15f71b4aa392b85947f993834f553aae99d58.gif[/img]

The first thing to do to release the epicness of a game is to work on the visual effects. So we've designed effects for each spell, item, summon, and enemy movement. Each animation must meet a few specific criteria:
[list]
[*] each animation must be unique and easily identifiable
[*] an animation must not interfere with the reading of stat changes (such as damage inflicted for example)
[*] the more powerful the effects, the more the animation should be strong 
[/list]

[b]Clear feedback[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/5f6a382fb8d8c6d50836181762bcb2d941eceeec.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/9f4a95965d62a382a272d033b749c453501817e8.gif[/img]

The other lever on which we can press to have epic and memorable fights is the feeling that the player can have with each action.

We have therefore particularly worked on feedback. The camera shakes depending on the damage inflicted or received, and the destroyed cards have a particular animation.

Also, the edges of the screen turn red when the player's life is below 50%. In the original game, this threshold was 25%, but our tests showed that this threshold was too low due to the low number of life points available to the player.

[b]Keep player active during opponent's turn[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/b5ac5acd608bc90bbc49d87d84ec362280fef31c.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/8d1bf66c8938acbd592118cc8f176c273aaf748e.gif[/img]

Fighting in Drifter's Tales is a test of strength and strategy. As such, we've changed the way to play during the opponent's turn pending player actions. He will no longer be passive and various tests of speed and skill will await him.

[b]Hidden mechanics[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/9b6ee58a04a6bcf763c29192828aa6a064a8f11b.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/9d5401814e06e96df8c7a7709e95003f92b61052.gif[/img]

In our alpha testing, we iterated around to find out which things we can do to increase tension, and it turned out that the number of hit points was the central thing - much more than the number of cards on the playing board.

So when the player's hitpoints are below 50%, the game becomes a bit easier. On the contrary, above this 50%, the game is a little more difficult and the player will lose the first half of his life quickly. The player therefore has the impression of being on the go and this creates tension during the fights.

notes.title: Dev diary #5: Alpha post-mortem, upcoming changes & Steam page
notes.content:
We launched our alpha version a few weeks ago and we already have a lot of interesting feedback on how our players have used our game.

If you would like to participate, you can register here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeaYRR1KQjarm1cZcuW6aHoCTA66PnAy1xuV-E9AWdCcht8tQ/viewform?usp=sf_link

Oh, and also we finally have our Steam page for our game! We will tell you a little more about it at the end of the article if you wish to wishlist us.

[b]Some metrics, and what they mean[/b]

In order to share with you the work we have done during these few weeks of watching you play, we have decided to share with you some metrics that we consider interesting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/75ef93dbf2bbdbc074a8a7e93bfe7ed3c32b049a.png[/img]

The first metric is the usage of stories in this alpha release. The first story to be chosen is undoubtedly the one called “Following the Footsteps”. We don't know (yet) if the main reason is that the button to choose this story is the first one, or if the story has a more welcoming title.

Also, the abandonment rate of stories after a failure is very low (around 11%), which is a good indicator for us!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/94c2a6a6a4bd8309ee9c7819d1338a24ef8982dd.png[/img]

The second important metric is on the use of the cards while battling. Unsurprisingly, creatures are the most used (because they are the most offensive), but a few secret cards were used (Gargoyle, The Wall and Break).

Also, spells and items are being used correctly, and we're very happy with how the fights are going.

[b]Changes to the game[/b]

We're going to do some small changes to the game in the coming weeks, based on your feedback and what we've noticed in your playing habits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/9c048621340085554b27037e9a66dee829d301c0.png[/img]

First, we are going to shuffle the order of the buttons while selecting a story. Thus, we will see if the discrepancy between the stories played is due to the position of the button, or to the title of the story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/3cc7cebd9ccfcfbbc7d5ddbe99862b333ae96c10.png[/img]

Then it occurred to us that the puzzles on the chests were too complicated and required knowledge of the game that new players don't have. We will therefore simplify them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/561bb0f65950e0008a865ae5764451f04f6a74dc.png[/img]

Also, we had a new review in the original game which we found to be very interesting. Enemy actions are not legible enough if they have a lot of text. We will therefore make the validation of these actions mandatory when they are presented to you for the first time.

[b]We are on Steam![/b]

And yes, we have - finally - our Steam page! You can find all the necessary information there and wishlist us at this address: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2366490/DRIFTERS_TALES__A_narrative_board_game/

We are going to participate in the Steam Next Fest next October!

notes.title: Dev diary #4: A sneak peek at the first stories
notes.content:
Last month, I had the pleasure to let you know how we will support the alpha version of Drifter's Tales. Today, it's time for you to discover the two stories that will be present in this alpha version that you can obtain by filling out this form: [url=https://forms.gle/Qyi2a7VBwKYciT7AA]https://forms.gle/Qyi2a7VBwKYciT7AA[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/b54f4e52de1e39c59d601f2ebb975857161ad016.png[/img]

In Drifter's Tales, you won't be able to play all the stories in one go. You will travel to the continent of Carmina, and you will have to choose where to go.

We have planned more than a dozen stories that all have unique features. The first stories you will be able to experience are those that we offer you to discover in the Alpha version.

[b]Following the footsteps[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/662455f0631baa5455231bd050644d7c2f953154.png[/img]

In this story, after losing your memory, you decide to follow footprints in the sand. There you will discover the desert of Melates, leader of the thieves faction in Carmina.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/ba7a3a09bd25d174c0dc54ea160d0d5904ef7882.png[/img]

This story will be an opportunity for you to discover the joys of combat with 3 different enemies. Each fight will have a unique setup - you will have the opportunity to experience different plateaus and different enemy behaviors.

[b]A far landmark[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/d2c23f6c6e15f50c51f286eed004f7d9175c41a0.png[/img]

Would you have preferred to follow another path? No problem, another story is available. In "A far landmark", you'll be heading towards a huge mountain, but a strange temple will stand in your way. It is the temple of Daïs, said the Lover.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/0eadf2f3d62c135abdf2067da4b14fa9c8da14b9.png[/img]

This temple will be filled with traps of all kinds that you will have to counter through tests. During a test, you will have to draw a number which will be between 0 and 9 - the latter must be less than your life (in case of an endurance test) or a number of cards of a certain type in your deck .

[b]But still…[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/02523f7df0a16546988471e9ee56130d94407881.png[/img]

You have noticed that the pawn representing you has several shapes. This is your origin, and it grants you a few extra cards. You can have 4 different origins, and each origin has three unlockable cards.

You can't choose where you come from - but in Drifter's Tales, you'll have the ability to choose your destiny.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/5b1f36327351abf7f1e42a59a884ef271a100958.png[/img]

Also, you may meet a strange character to whom you can swear. In order to keep your promise, you will have to (or not do) a particular action to win an extra card at the end of the story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/2aec60d54bc0ec40eca0e773dd00f8ad82c0cbef.png[/img]

Finally (but that's not all we put in these stories, there is a lot to discover!) there is a small chance - or bad luck - that you will come across a random encounter. You will also have the opportunity to choose which encounter to draw according to three randomly chosen possibilities.

These are only a small part of the possibilities available to you in these stories. You can also find chests, solve puzzles and discover some well-hidden secrets.

We put a lot of love into this game that we've been building since last October, and we hope it will meet your expectations. We've compiled all your feedbacks from the first game to produce this brand new proposal and we're very happy to have the chance to improve! And this is thanks to you!

notes.title: Dev diary #3: Private alpha & support plan
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

The release date of the first private alpha is approaching and it's time to show you how we will support this version. Today no screenshots or fancy images. He are going to talk about telemetry, data and cakes.

Yes, about cakes.

As a reminder, you can participate in this alpha at this address: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeaYRR1KQjarm1cZcuW6aHoCTA66PnAy1xuV-E9AWdCcht8tQ/viewform?usp=sf_link  

[b]The usefulness of tracking actions[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/327f3101ce88aa4f57b4ac6a1d31f81cb59a0411.png[/img]

Since we deployed the first version of the online counterpart of our board game, we have developed our own telemetry system called “Solid Pancake”. Behind this name automatically generated by Github (thanks a lot for this legendary name) hides an event-based tracking system.

It's not an easy exercise, but I'll try to explain how this telemetry works. Each time you launch Drifter's Tales, the game informs our Solid Pancake service that a new session has been opened. This session has information about the product (not you), such as platform (Windows, Switch, etc.) and current product version. Then, with each action you take, we send a signal to the telemetry service so that we can know what you are doing.

So when you play a card, choose an action or win, we are able to analyze it all in order to balance the game and give you the best possible experience.

Here is a small overview of what we collect:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/350defdd244edb542d81c6e4dc68f32854adbe96.png[/img]

This tracking will be actively used during the private alpha to detect any issues that may arise during this test.

Solid Pancake is of course an open source project that you can build yourself on your own server: https://github.com/thefirstspine/solid-pancake  

[b]From collecting to display via Looker Studio[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/241f02f0d48300e90ca5f2b961202735936895d1.png[/img]

Tracking user actions is one thing. Being able to do something about it is another. For this we have set up what is called an ETL (Extract Transform Load). This ETL is responsible of transforming the data we have to be able to make a more usable and readable version of it in a visualization system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/26bb61b1f56572516b3438113d52619afce1a621.png[/img]

In order to visualize the data we use Google Looker Studio, which allows us to display relevant data about your experience. Here's some examples about what we can have:

[list]
[*] story completion rate
[*] rate of discovering secrets and oaths
[*] most played cards, most discarded cards
[*] hardest, easiest stories
[*] etc.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/a01900d015787d7f4aa8d357e8e771a5d887bc9b.png[/img]

[b]Private Alpha Support & Distribution Plan[/b]

With all this data, we will be able to have qualified feedbacks on the experience of the testers.

The private alpha will be sent to you via a Google Drive link to the email address you provided in the form. It will be maintained until the end of December, where all the issues and improvements will be pushed with monthly updates.

I sincerely hope that you will be satisfied with this relaunch of Drifter's Tales. Believe me when I tell you that we are more than excited to have your first feedback!

See you soon !

notes.title: Dev diary #2: A look of the new cards
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/a00d31564c2f932143b00b417fdc8c86f3899634.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

Last month I talked to you about the struggles and issues inherent in transposing a paper board game to a video game format. This month, it's time to take a closer look at some of the cards in the game, as well as the different ways to get them.

[h1]Some explanations on the cards[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/66a548ac803b2c214f9f0e0d8c81f61c54a50780.png[/img]

In Drifter's Tales you have many cards with various and original effects. Each card has its statistics as well as its effects. Each side of a card has a strength (in red) and a defense (in blue), with the number in the center representing the total hit points the card has.

For example, the Cyclops Statue card is not very powerful (one and only one life point, no strength, no defense), but once placed on the board, it grants you gems in order to add some money to your purse.

[h1]How to get cards in a story[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/d42e0e40f55465bbdc004ccfb4963881896fc46e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/7d0482ec9714f2f90ee258ff932532be2e63c95d.png[/img]

There are many ways to get cards in a story!

Among these are random encounters that can occur during your game at any time. Each encounter allows you to have one or more new cards in a different way.

For example, the Broken Mirror encounter allows you to obtain the Duplicate card, at the cost of a wait that could be... somewhat fatal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/cf16d0bb395ed48ababe72bd8af7c50dc2de2c32.png[/img]

Then, each story has one or more chests. These chests contain a puzzle to solve and - if you succeed - you will get a random card from a pool of 5 cards.

One of the cards you can get, Replacement, allows you to replace any of your cards on the game board with another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/1091e493b8e6684ed653f3e487c6766a4fc2e0c3.png[/img]

Other means are at your disposal to get new cards. Many secrets are scattered throughout the game, allowing you to add new cards to your collection. For example, you may meet important characters asking you to take an oath that you must respect. But beware: woe to you if you betray your oath!

[h1]Upgrade your cards[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/8ee8726b637b2984d3b51e54eb2071289dfce017.png[/img]

At the end of a story, you will also be able to upgrade the base cards of your starting deck to a more powerful version. Thus, the Banshee could be replaced by the Banshee of Mara.

Each of your basic cards will be replaced by this improved version, and your choice will be very important for the fights to come!

[h1]The collection[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/7a1d89d1a3329d9cd9debcdf28e3d356830138bf.png[/img]

The original game had 35 cards. Although for some players this number could seem limited, I find that it is a sufficient number for a game with a lifespan of a few hours. Reviews of the original game were taken in account, and I added some 50 more cards, increasing the total number of playing cards to 85.

Your collection will have over fifty unlockable cards across all of your saves, and - who knows - you'll discover a secret that I put there.

[h1]Next month[/h1]

Next month, I will tell you about the first private alpha to collect all your feedback! Because - indeed - I really need to playtest this version before going to production. If you are interested in this test, here is the registration link: [url=https://forms.gle/w4GPCauoSgitTibZ6]https://forms.gle/w4GPCauoSgitTibZ6[/url]  - your name will be credited at the end of the game!

notes.title: Dev diary #1: Let’s have a look on the battles
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/8ee1dcaf00afa308fbae88ea4bcc5b68eab52736.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

Today has come the day I am ready to write a devlog. Devlog that will allow hikers to discover the game I've been working on for a few years, but also to collect your feedback on the few screenshots that illustrate this article.

[h1]It all started with a board game presented in Europe[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/90bd874444abdf83a991650d95f35d43f063d2f8.png[/img]

It’s been a few years (I'm talking about the pre-pandemic era, yes) since I've been presenting the prototype of my board game that I'm trying to publish and finance. The rules are relatively simple: you play as a wizard, and you must place cards with various statistics (life, strength, defense) on a game board to reach your opponent.

To finance this project, I therefore decided to develop and sell a dematerialized solo version of this game, by developing the lore hidden in the cards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/7be7caf091af950e84f849403bb720a0fd7e1919.png[/img]

Thus was born Drifter's Tales: a narrative board game that gives pride of place to storytelling and discovery. But today, we're going to focus on the major challenge inherent in this transformation: moving from a 2-4 day competitive game to a single-player game.

[h1]This game is a solo version - I had to adapt it[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/33821413df5996e3f2fe7e4f7adbc46caaadc2b0.png[/img]

First challenge: how the enemies that the player will have to fight should behave? I tested a few variations, like having a different deck for each enemy (and believe me, it took a while) or having pre-determined patterns that repeat over and over.

It is this last proposition I chose. First, because the development would have been really tedious - like a real complexity nightmare - and then because the player must be able to end each fight in 5 minutes, and not in 30 minutes as the original game offers.

Thus, each enemy has from 2 to 5 moves available, which the player can anticipate using these icons at the top right of the screen:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/1ae08fc769aaaf27fc5ba87e2cb32019b57d5b1b.png[/img]

So the enemy can place & move cards, play spells or use any kind of threat against you. Each threat can of course be thwarted with the right strategy.

The second challenge - and not the least - is about the readability. How to display the statistics of the cards on a large game board, while giving the possibility of having an overview on this same board?

At first, I had focused on a zoom function, but zooming in on the cards was detracting from the readability of the big picture. Then this zoom became optional, with pressing a key that would activate an “assistance” mode. But the tests were not conclusive, the player having to continuously activate and deactivate this mode.

A third option - and this is the one I chose - is to give the player the possibility to change their point of view, from the view of their hand to a view of the whole board:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/d89957a997472554daef7ff3e3f0142e3ee916ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/d75e7066fe085a233248ec1e50b6336e3f2b5938.png[/img]

[h1]Going further thanks to the video game medium[/h1]

Freeing myself from the rules established by the paper game was really beneficial from a game design point of view. Thus, some enemies have movements that make the player interact directly, such as avoiding projectiles sent by the opponent:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/d40abb929c426c426f9b54f4b57ea246ef4f3835.png[/img]

Of course, I developed other interactions to change from a variation on the shoot 'em up: runes to draw with the keys of the keyboard or memorize a series of symbols.

[h1]I need testers for an alpha version[/h1]

In order to properly test the game in alpha I need testers. Balancing the difficulty or even finding bugs is something tedious and counterproductive (as you can miss many things) when you are alone. Thus, I share a form where you can register for an alpha which will be released at the end of June here: https://forms.gle/hQg14wD97FPuS5T96

Thank you all for this long read, I hope it was instructive for you (if you are a solo dev like me) and that it made you want to know more!

And as we say around here: à plus dans le bus!

[b]By testing new things in Drifter's Tales thanks to your feedbacks, we now have many improvements for you by completely redesigning our narrative version of The First Spine.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/563124ee14b43fe2aa4563e82be20f2c81a15ed6.png[/img]

[h3]We know that the first draft is perfectible. That's why the first adventure will be available as additional content, taking advantage of all the improvements we're going to make. This content will be free for all players who have a registered account on The First Spine before February 1st.[/h3]

[h1]A brand new exploration[/h1]

We have completely redesigned the exploration. From now on, your position is materialized by a pawn that you can move. You will then be able to choose the cards you draw and you will no longer have to read the texts of the cards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/39f62db8b481656dfebb95e94a78ff3745963e9d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/25d08a7691357002fdf694531c7cb24c004d7b74.png[/img]

[h1]More cards available[/h1]

30 new cards will be added to the game.

These cards are taken from the origins classes of the base game and feature new mechanics, such as the modification of the board during the fights. New ways to obtain cards have also been integrated into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/243013569adf1e1859f61bdcac63c82bb7faa03b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/59b64e428e4935ea58eafcc82d6883dbdcc70433.png[/img]

[h1]Redesigned battles[/h1]

We have also decided to take over the combat mechanics entirely. Thus, all the fights will be done directly on the game area without any loading or waiting time.

Finally, most of the enemy's movements will require dexterity: you will not remain idle during the opponent's turn!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/dc54a4a5f9d58aac69ba0ce2a4d96f09e2c41f04.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/5b19dee4c1ba8ca0d948a92a5f423633c9cf94d3.png[/img]

[h1]We give you access to our private alpha[/h1]

We will put our community at the center of all the decisions we will make! Who better than you to give us an opinion on the game that [b]you[/b] are going to play?

In order to access the private alpha version next June, simply fill out this form:

[h2][url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeaYRR1KQjarm1cZcuW6aHoCTA66PnAy1xuV-E9AWdCcht8tQ/viewform]Private alpha registration[/url][/h2]

notes.title: About the november 3 update
notes.content:
The November update is fast approaching, and now we can tell you more. Discover new cards and new ways to customize your deck.

[b]New UI on card exclusion[/b]

By studying the telemetry data, it appeared to us that the exclusion of cards - which is a feature requested by most of you - is rarely used. We have therefore chosen to highlight it more when selecting stories.

Also, the very last story will no longer play automatically, allowing you to exclude cards from your deck.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/edbf3e4fe25b0bca3fbe234ab7ae2e32d9729eba.png[/img]

[b]New cards and a valuation of mana stones[/b]

We also noticed that the mana stones were not used very much. Blame it on a hazardous object, whose usefulness comes down to having more cards in the deck at the end of a story.

Thus, we decided to modify this object. There are now 3 types of stones, each of which can move a card from your discard pile directly into your hand (and no longer into the deck). During the tests of this functionality, it appeared that this novelty also increased the synergies between the cards and greatly facilitated the understanding of this object.

Finally, new cards will appear, allowing you - among other things - to directly duplicate cards on the board, modify the statistics of enemies or even give you the possibility of placing more than one card per turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/b743f4e764177d8424583a2294b808b6197216b6.png[/img]

[b]Buy cards you already have[/b]

Always with the aim of providing you with a complete card game experience, we have added a new character that allows you to buy cards that have already been acquired. This character will offer you 6 cards for sale each time you talk to him. To make it easier for you, we have rebalanced the whole economy of the game. So you will have more gems to buy these cards and also buy upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/cf51c24968a4e4df6494bbb0d9537f135954ed45.png[/img]

[b]Do not restart a story from the beginning[/b]

Still studying the telemetry data, we realized that a large number of players left the game after a failure. We have therefore added checkpoints in each story, allowing you to no longer start from the beginning with each failure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/6e1a6d0d0802cf0622bd98559116510472f16e2b.png[/img]

[b]Random events to surprise you[/b]

This update contains some random events. These events will allow you to have new cards, always serving the narrative. These encounters will not be visible while exploring and will trigger automatically when you go to certain cards. We don't want to reveal too much, but each encounter has a price to pay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/47b825fe6055823d4ca4410630bcc45352382a66.png[/img]

[b]...and many other quality of life improvements[/b]

And that's not all. We're also going to include a lot of quality of life improvements on this update, here's a quick snippet:
[list]
[*] Better support for all screen resolutions
[*] The defense of some enemies has been reduced in The Village story
[*] Sellers were added in the last story
[*] Added feedback when purchasing items
[*] The illustrations of Jester and Gargoyle have been revamped
[*] Zoom on cards in the menu & the exclusion screen have been increased
[*] The transition speed when a card is chosen while exploring has been increased
[*] Bets have been raised on all stories
[/list]

[b]And then?[/b]

From now on I will use the pronoun "I", and no longer "we". Because indeed, I am the only developer on this game.

I've been in a period of intense development for 14 weeks, and I'm starting to tire. The Switch port also requires a lot of effort from me and I think it's time for me to rest and watch what happens for the December update.

I tried to offer you the best possible game with my means, and the effort / positive impact ratio is currently too low to continue to include new features. The December update will therefore only offer bug fixes.

Drifter's Tales was launched too soon, that's a fact. However, the free early access phase showed us that the game was ready given the quality of the feedback you posted. The ball is now in your court: if you appreciate the efforts I put into this game, I invite you to talk about it around you to encourage this long-term project.

Teddy

notes.title: Exiting the Early Access phase
notes.content:
We are happy to release the game from its early access phase and bring you the last three stories of the game! These stories have never-before-seen features and we hope you enjoy them.

Note that the price of the game now goes to 9.90€. If you have installed the early version, the game will remain free.

[list]
[*] New story: The Moss
[*] New Story: The Stone
[*] New Story: The Monarch
[*] New Covenant: Followers of Mara
[*] New Covenant: The Mother of Lost Faith
[/list]

[b]What are we going to do in the future?[/b]

We will rest and support the game by only releasing quality of life improvements and bug fixes until the end of July. After this well-deserved rest, we will turn to free additional content that will highlight certain aspects of the game:
[list]
[*] New game +, new game +2 - after the end of the game, you can choose to restart a game keeping your level and acquired items. New cards can be unlocked, and enemies will have additional cards in their deck.
[*] Ghostly Cards - in each story you will have the option to send other players cards with unique effects along with a message. These cards can be unlocked randomly at the end of the fights.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42167009/62c4a74b5dce17d1ec6a9faa4a6b6c44ede24626.png[/img]

As you can see from the roadmap above, this additional content has been planned for release in early October. We won't reveal too much about what this new version will contain, but it could well give a particular direction to a future project that we have in the boxes.

[b]And above all…[/b]

Thanks. Thank you for supporting this game while it was being designed and finished, we received lots of positive feedback, as well as a ton of community feedback which helped the game to have this quality that we are proud of.

We don't have the media coverage or the budget of some games, but it's been a real pleasure to dive into this adventure - and it will be a pleasure to continue it with you.

notes.content:
Now you can tip the developers of Drifter's Tales to continue development of the game until the final version scheduled for September.

Purchasing this DLC will add a new card to your inventory: The Thank which will grant you 1 life point permanently. But that's not all ! You will have the possibility to appear in the end credits with the name you want!

[b]You can buy this DLC here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1950880/Drifters_Tales__Early_Access_tip_for_developers/[/b]
